questions.question: What does polymorphism mean in C++?
questions.explanation: Polymorphism means 'many forms'. In C++, the same interface or name can behave differently in different situations.

questions.question: What are the two main types of polymorphism in C++?
questions.explanation: The two main types are static (compile-time) polymorphism and dynamic (run-time) polymorphism.

questions.question: Which type of polymorphism is resolved at compile time?
questions.explanation: Compile-time polymorphism is resolved by the compiler before the program runs. Function overloading and operator overloading are common examples.

questions.question: Which type of polymorphism is also known as static polymorphism?
questions.explanation: Compile-time polymorphism is also called static polymorphism because the function or operation is determined at compile time.

questions.question: Which type of polymorphism is also known as dynamic polymorphism?
questions.explanation: Run-time polymorphism is also called dynamic polymorphism because the appropriate function is selected during program execution.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of compile-time polymorphism?
questions.explanation: Function overloading is resolved at compile time, so it is a form of compile-time polymorphism.

questions.question: Which of the following is another common example of compile-time polymorphism?
questions.explanation: Operator overloading allows operators such as + or == to work with user-defined objects and is resolved at compile time.

questions.question: Which feature is commonly used to achieve run-time polymorphism in C++?
questions.explanation: Virtual functions enable dynamic dispatch, which is the basis of run-time polymorphism in C++.

questions.question: Compile-time polymorphism is also associated with which type of binding?
questions.explanation: In compile-time polymorphism, the function call is determined early, during compilation. Therefore it is called early or static binding.

questions.question: Run-time polymorphism is associated with which type of binding?
questions.explanation: In run-time polymorphism, the appropriate overridden function is selected during execution, so it is called late or dynamic binding.

questions.question: Which keyword is used to declare a virtual function in C++?
questions.explanation: The virtual keyword tells C++ that a member function can be overridden in a derived class and dynamically dispatched.

questions.question: Which concept allows a derived class to provide its own implementation of a base class virtual function?
questions.explanation: Function overriding occurs when a derived class provides a new implementation of a virtual function inherited from the base class.

questions.question: Run-time polymorphism generally requires which relationship between classes?
questions.explanation: Run-time polymorphism commonly works through inheritance, where a base-class pointer or reference refers to a derived-class object.

questions.question: What is dynamic binding?
options: Selecting the appropriate overridden function at run time
Creating an object at compile time
questions.explanation: Dynamic binding means the actual function to execute is determined at run time, typically through a virtual function.

questions.question: What is early binding?
questions.explanation: Early binding means the function call is resolved at compile time. It is commonly associated with static polymorphism.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes compile-time polymorphism?
options: It is resolved during program execution
It is resolved by the compiler
questions.explanation: The compiler determines which overloaded function or operator should be used during compilation.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes run-time polymorphism?
options: It is always resolved by the compiler
It is achieved only through function overloading
questions.explanation: Run-time polymorphism commonly uses inheritance and virtual functions to select the correct overridden function during execution.

questions.question: Consider: class Base { public: virtual void show(); }; What is the main purpose of 'virtual' here?
questions.explanation: The virtual keyword enables dynamic dispatch when the function is called through a suitable base-class pointer or reference.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT normally considered an example of compile-time polymorphism?
questions.explanation: Virtual function overriding is associated with run-time polymorphism, while function and operator overloading are compile-time mechanisms.

questions.question: Which keyword can be used in a derived class to explicitly indicate that a function overrides a virtual base-class function?
questions.explanation: The override specifier helps the compiler verify that the derived-class function correctly overrides a virtual function from the base class.

questions.question: What is a pure virtual function?
questions.explanation: A pure virtual function is declared using = 0, for example: virtual void show() = 0;

questions.question: A class containing at least one pure virtual function is generally called what?
questions.explanation: A class with at least one pure virtual function is an abstract class and cannot be directly instantiated.

questions.question: Can an object of an abstract class be created directly?
questions.explanation: An abstract class cannot be directly instantiated because it contains at least one pure virtual function that has no complete implementation in the base class.
